The '''1920 German football championship''', the 13th edition of the competition, was won by [[1. FC Nürnberg]], defeating [[SpVgg Fürth]] 2–0 in the final. It was the first edition of the championship after the [[First World War]] and was staged six years after the previous championship in 1914.<ref name="Rsssf" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html |title=German championship 1920 |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 8 January 2016}}</ref>

For 1. FC Nürnberg it was the first national championship and was the start of Nuremberg's most successful era where the club won five titles in eight seasons from 1920 to 1927, missing out on a sixth one in the inconclusive 1922 championship. Fürth, the defending champions, would go on to win the 1926 and 1929 championship. It was the only encounter of the two [[Middle Franconia]]n rivals in the final.<ref name="List" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html |title=(West) Germany -List of champions |website= Rsssf.com |access-date= 8 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/1-fc-nuernberg/1/ |title= 1. FC Nürnberg » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= 1. FC Nürnberg honours}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/spvgg-greuther-fuerth/1/ |title= SpVgg Greuther Fürth » Steckbrief |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=SpVgg Greuther Fürth honours}}</ref>

Nürnberg's [[Heinrich Träg]] and Fürth's [[Leonhard Seiderer|Lony Seiderer]] and [[Viktor Hierländer]] were the top scorer of the 1920 championship with four goals each.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 8 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

Eight clubs qualified for the knock-out competition, the champions of each of the seven regional football championships and the defending German champions.<ref name="Rsssf" />
